faults.quote: used as a directional complement after other verbs to indicate completion or movement downward
faults.why: In 拿掉 and 忘掉, 掉 is a resultative complement indicating removal/disappearance, not downward movement.

faults.quote: My phone dropped on the ground.
faults.why: Unnatural English; 'fell on the ground' or 'dropped to the ground' is natural.
